few adjective

also not many, very few, fewer, few people

classical

Cic. Amic. 2: paucī admodum familiārēs
Traupman 314

paucī, paucae, pauca

adjective, plural; comparative pauciōrēs

few, a few

“Few” and “a few” alike: paucīs diēbus, in a few days. As a noun, paucī are few people, a handful, and pauca a few words: Paucīs tē volō, “a quick word with you” (Ter. And. 29). The singular is very rare (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • rārus, rāra, rārum — few and far between, scattered; rare

    also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.118: adpārent rārī nantēs in gurgite vastō

    Few in the sense of thinly spread, here and there; also rare, uncommon.

Examples

  • paucīs temeritās est bonō, multīs malō

    rashness turns out well for a few, and badly for manyPhaedr. 5.4.12

  • Paucōrum est intellegere, quid dōnet diēs.

    Few understand what the day is giving.Publ. P 53

See also many, couple, a lot.
